subtitle: A Mother Carves an Empire into Stone

panels.shot: low-angle wide of a dim rock-cut hall with towering pillars, Gautami Balashri in the foreground touching a chisel-marked wall
panels.action: Gautami Balashri stands in Nashik Cave 3, aged yet steady, her hand resting on a freshly carved inscription that gleams faintly in the lamplight of the rock-cut vihara.

dialogue.text: In the 19th year of Pulumavi, a mother named Gautami Balashri carved into stone a eulogy so fierce that it still argues with history.

i18n.hi: पुलुमावि के उन्नीसवें साल में गौतमी बालश्री नाम की माँ ने पत्थर पर ऐसा उग्र स्तुति‑लेख तराशा कि आज भी इतिहास से बहस करता है।

panels.shot: slow push-in from cave entrance, framing Balashri against shadowed pillars and monks' cells
panels.action: From the sunlit mouth of Nashik Cave 3, we see Gautami Balashri inside, wrapped in a simple but rich sari, framed by orderly cells and massive pillars of the vihara.

dialogue.text: This cave in the hills above Nasik was once a humming vihara. But its most enduring echo is not a monk’s sermon, it is a mother’s voice in stone.

i18n.hi: नासिक की पहाड़ियों की यह गुफा कभी गूंजता हुआ विहार थी, पर इसकी सबसे लंबी गूंज न भिक्षु का उपदेश है, नाद है पत्थर बनी एक माँ की आवाज़।

panels.shot: medium close-up on Balashri’s face, half-lit by a bronze oil lamp
panels.action: Gautami Balashri sits near the wall, an oil lamp by her side, her lined face calm yet intent, eyes following the artisan’s chisel strokes.

dialogue.text: She is Gautami Balashri, mother of Gautamiputra Satakarni, grandmother of King Vasishthiputra Pulumavi. Not a legend, but a name we can still read.

i18n.hi: वह है गौतमी बालश्री — गौतमीपुत्र सातकर्णी की माँ, राजा वशिष्ठिपुत्र पुलुमावि की दादी; कोई गाथा नहीं, एक नाम जो आज भी पढ़ा जा सकता है।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder from behind Balashri, looking toward the wall with faint incised letters taking shape
panels.action: From behind Gautami Balashri’s shoulder we see the rock face, lines of Brahmi letters just emerging as the artisan carves them into the smoothened stone.

dialogue.text: Her inscription in Cave Three begins as many grants do, with date and king. But soon the words swell into something else: a prashasti, a rolling wave of praise.

i18n.hi: गुफा तीन का उसका लेख शुरू होता है जैसे और दानपत्र होते हैं — तिथि और राजा से; पर थोड़ी ही दूर शब्द उमड़ कर बन जाते हैं प्रशस्ति, लहराती हुई स्तुति।

panels.shot: wide shot of the cave interior, monks and artisans faintly visible as silhouettes, Balashri central
panels.action: Artisans chip at the wall while a couple of Buddhist monks pass quietly in the background; Gautami Balashri remains seated in the middle ground, a small figure amidst vast stone.

dialogue.text: The record calls this the 19th year of her grandson Pulumavi. Yet the heart of the text looks back, to her son’s battles, her son’s titles, her son’s gifts.

i18n.hi: लेख इसे उसके पोते पुलुमावि का उन्नीसवाँ वर्ष कहता है, पर दिल पूरा मुड़ जाता है पीछे — बेटे के युद्धों, उपाधियों, दानों की ओर।

panels.shot: close-up of Balashri’s hands resting on her lap, fingers lightly touching a folded palm-leaf manuscript
panels.action: Her hands, veined but steady, rest on a rolled palm-leaf manuscript, suggesting a prepared text, as she listens to the carved words being murmured back to her.

dialogue.text: She has not come unprepared. The phrases, polished and formal, are likely drafted before the rock is touched. This is not mere memory; it is public performance.

i18n.hi: वह खाली हाथ नहीं आई; तराशे हुए, दरबारी वाक्य शायद पहले ही लिखे गए थे — यह सिर्फ याद नहीं, खुला सार्वजनिक प्रदर्शन है।

panels.shot: medium profile shot of Balashri, lips slightly parted as if dictating, artisan in foreground carving
panels.action: In profile, Gautami Balashri leans slightly forward, speaking with measured authority while an artisan in the foreground drives his chisel into the rock.

dialogue.speaker: gautami_balashri
dialogue.text: Write of him as my son… but also as protector of this land.

i18n.hi: उसे मेरे बेटे की तरह लिखो… पर साथ ही इस धरती के रक्षक की तरह भी।

panels.shot: tight shot on the inscription area showing early lines; camera angled so a few legible letters suggest Brahmi without being fully readable
panels.action: The chisel point bites into the polished rock, forming neat Brahmi characters in horizontal lines, while stone dust catches the lamplight.

dialogue.text: The lines call Gautamiputra ‘eka-bamhana’—the solitary or unique Brahmana. Later scholars will argue over the phrase, but the pride in it is unmistakable.

i18n.hi: पंक्तियाँ गौतमीपुत्र को ‘एक‑ब्रह्मण’ कहती हैं — अकेला, अनोखा ब्राह्मण; बाद के पंडित अर्थ पर लड़ेंगे, पर इसमें झलकता गर्व साफ है।

panels.shot: medium shot with imaginative backdrop: Balashri in present foreground, while faint, ghostly outline of a battle scene occupies the background
panels.action: As Gautami Balashri watches the carving, a faint overlaid scene behind her suggests armoured warriors on elephants and horsemen riding hard across a dusty plain.

dialogue.text: She has the victories carved large: her son, it proclaims, broke the pride of Sakas, Yavanas, Pahlavas, humbled foreign lords and restored the Satavahana name.

i18n.hi: वह विजयाएँ मोटे अक्षरों में खुदवाती है — लेख ऐलान करता है कि उसके बेटे ने शकों, यवनों, पहलवों का मान तोड़ा, परकीय शासकों को झुकाया, सातवाहन नाम फिर उठाया।

panels.shot: low-angle dramatic shot of Balashri as if addressing unseen courtiers, with map-like mountains faint in the background
panels.action: Seen from a low angle, Gautami Balashri slightly raises her chin, while behind her the artist hints at stylised ranges and rivers suggesting Deccan, Vidarbha, Andhra lands.

dialogue.text: The inscription names wide territories under his sway. But historians read with care: a prashasti stretches space as it stretches adjectives.

i18n.hi: शिलालेख कई फैले हुए प्रदेश उसके अधिकार में गिनता है, पर इतिहासकार धीमे पढ़ते हैं — प्रशस्ति जैसे विशेषण बढ़ाती है, वैसे ही फैलाती है सीमा।

panels.shot: medium shot of Balashri and a Buddhist monk seated opposite each other near a pillar
panels.action: Later, Gautami Balashri sits speaking quietly with a shaven-headed monk in simple robes, the cave pillar rising between them like a witness.

dialogue.text: Yet this is not only a war-song. In the same stone she records grants to these monks, the feeding of the sangha, the building of cells and walks for the rainy season.

i18n.hi: और यह सिर्फ युद्ध‑गीत नहीं; इसी पत्थर में वह भिक्षुओं को दान, संघ का भोजन, वर्षा‑ऋतु के लिए कुटियों और पथों का निर्माण भी दर्ज करती है।

panels.shot: close-up on Balashri’s face, a slight softening in her eyes, background blurring
panels.action: Her expression softens, eyes moist yet controlled, as if remembering both the weight of kingship and the fragility of life.

dialogue.text: Between lines of conquest, the prashasti names virtues: generosity, discipline, truthfulness. It praises her son as much for restraint as for the reach of his arm.

i18n.hi: विजयों की पंक्तियों के बीच प्रशस्ति गुण गिनती है — दानशीलता, संयम, सत्य; वह उसके बेटे को उतना ही संयम के लिए सराहती है जितना बाँहों की पहुँच के लिए।

panels.shot: medium shot where Balashri gestures to the artisan to include lines about herself
panels.action: Gautami Balashri gently lifts a hand, indicating a space on the wall, the artisan pausing to listen, slight surprise in his eyes.

dialogue.text: Then, quietly, she has her own qualities set down: devoted wife, firm in vows, giver of gifts. A woman refusing to vanish behind her men.

i18n.hi: फिर, धीरे से, वह अपने गुण भी लिखवाती है — पति परायण, व्रतों में दृढ़, दान देने वाली; वह औरत जो अपने पुरुषों के पीछे गायब होने से इनकार करती है।

panels.shot: wide shot showing Balashri, artisans, and a few onlookers including a Satavahana official
panels.action: A Satavahana official in courtly attire stands observing near the entrance, while artisans work and Gautami Balashri remains seated, the subtle center of authority in the scene.

dialogue.text: Her role is powerful, public, but not a formal queen on the throne. The inscription’s power lies instead in patronage, in who may speak for the dynasty in stone.

i18n.hi: उसकी भूमिका तेज है, सार्वजनिक है, पर राजसिंहासन पर औपचारिक रानी नहीं; इस लेख की ताकत है संरक्षण में, कि राजवंश की ओर से पत्थर पर कौन बोल सकता है।

panels.shot: overhead shot of the cave floor, with Balashri rising slowly, lamp casting a long shadow
panels.action: From above, we see Gautami Balashri rising to her feet, the oil lamp beside her stretching her shadow long across the stone floor toward the carved wall.

dialogue.speaker: gautami_balashri
dialogue.text: Let those yet unborn know his name… and mine with his.

i18n.hi: जो अभी जन्मे भी नहीं, वे भी उसका नाम जानें… और उसके साथ मेरा भी।

panels.shot: slow push-in on the finished inscription surface, Balashri’s silhouette small at the edge
panels.action: The camera moves closer to the now-complete panel of writing, while Gautami Balashri’s small silhouette is seen departing toward the cave’s sunlit opening.

dialogue.text: When she steps away, the work is done. Her son is gone, her grandson reigns, but their story, filtered through her words, has been fixed into the hill itself.

i18n.hi: जब वह पीछे हटती है, काम पूरा हो चुका है — बेटा चला गया, पोता राज कर रहा है, पर उनकी कथा उसके शब्दों में छनकर खुद पहाड़ में जड़ हो गई है।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide shot: the cave mouth seen across centuries, with subtle hints of changing visitors
panels.action: The cave entrance is shown as a constant frame, while faint superimposed figures of traders, pilgrims, colonial-era scholars, and modern visitors drift across the foreground.

dialogue.text: Centuries pass. Empires rise and crumble. Yet readers in distant ages will bend over this wall, still hearing Gautami Balashri speak across two thousand years.

i18n.hi: सदियाँ बीतती हैं, साम्राज्य उठते‑टूटते हैं, पर दूर के युगों के पाठक झुककर इस दीवार को पढ़ेंगे, दो हज़ार साल बाद भी गौतमी बालश्री की आवाज़ सुनते हुए।

panels.shot: extreme close-up on a few clear Brahmi letters of her name, then pulling back to reveal the broader inscription
panels.action: We see a tight focus on carved letters forming her own name, then the view pulls back to show how it sits among lines of royal titles and boasts.

dialogue.text: To us, her eulogy is both window and warning: a crafted royal boast, not a literal map, yet one of the clearest, earliest women’s voices in Indian political history.

i18n.hi: हमारे लिए उसकी स्तुति एक खिड़की भी है, चेतावनी भी — गढ़ा हुआ शाही घमंड, सचमुच का नक्शा नहीं, पर भारतीय राजनीतिक इतिहास में औरत की सबसे साफ, प्राचीन आवाज़ों में एक।

panels.shot: final contemplative shot of modern sky above the Nashik hills, faint overlay of Balashri’s calm face
panels.action: Above the rugged Nashik hills, the open sky stretches wide; faintly, the serene face of Gautami Balashri hovers like a memory over the landscape.

dialogue.text: In her hands, a mother’s grief and pride became statecraft. She reminds us that sometimes the sharpest chisel on a king’s fame is not his sword, but a woman’s inscription.

i18n.hi: उसके हाथों में एक माँ का शोक और गर्व राज्यकला बन गया; वह याद दिलाती है कि कई बार राजा की कीर्ति पर सबसे पैना औजार उसकी तलवार नहीं, किसी औरत का शिलालेख होता है।

title_i18n.en: The Mother's Eulogy in Cave Three
title_i18n.hi: गुफा तीन में माँ की शिलालेख स्तुति

subtitle_i18n.en: A Mother Carves an Empire into Stone
subtitle_i18n.hi: एक माँ ने पत्थर पर गढ़ा अपना सम्राज्य
